article.hook: It’s not a fear of being hurt - it’s the fear of losing control when someone gets too close. Chiron in Scorpio stirs the old ache around trust and power, making intimacy feel like a tightrope walk without a net.
article.lived: Chiron moves through Scorpio slowly, carving out seven to eight years for this wound to live and breathe. We notice it in the sharp pause before opening up, the way conversations around feelings circle the same guarded corners, and the silent test of how much vulnerability someone will accept before pulling back. It’s the quiet moment when you decide whether to let someone past your locked door or keep it shut for another season.
article.turn: This wound flips when holding tight to control becomes a fortress. The same walls built to protect end up blocking all entrances - no one close enough to heal, no one close enough to hurt. You don’t fix this by pushing trust harder; you fix it by learning where your limits are without letting them turn into cages.
moves: Name one boundary that feels necessary and explain why you need it.
Offer a small, nonverbal sign of trust and watch how it lands.
Notice when you pull away and say aloud what you’re protecting.
